Ambrish Kumar Pandey

I study palaeomagnetism, rock magnetism, and impact cratering, with a focus on how impact-generated shock waves alter the magnetic properties of crystalline rocks. My research uses the Dhala Impact Structure, India, as a case study to investigate the magnetic signatures of impact processes.

01 · About

Research Profile

Academic background, research direction and broader scientific interests.

I am currently a FARE Fellow (postdoctoral researcher) in the Department of Earth Sciences at the Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur, having submitted my Ph.D. thesis. My academic background is in geological sciences, with specialized expertise in palaeomagnetism, rock magnetism, and impact cratering.

My research focuses on the magnetic response of impactites and target rocks from the Dhala Impact Structure, India, with broader implications for planetary magnetism. I combine laboratory-based magnetic measurements, mineralogical characterization, and field-based geological investigations to understand how impact processes modify magnetic minerals and remanent magnetization.

PhD thesis · submitted
Effects of shock waves on magnetic properties of crystalline rocks: A case study from the Dhala Impact Structure, IndiaAdvisor: Dr. Amar Agarwal, Associate Professor, Department of Earth Sciences, IIT Kanpur
02 · Research

Research focus

Key questions and approaches in my current and related research.

Paleomagnetism

Investigation of remanent magnetization and paleomagnetic directions preserved in target rocks and impactites.

Rock magnetism

Characterization of magnetic minerals and their response to shock, thermal and geological processes.

Impact cratering

Magnetic and structural evidence for impact-related deformation, impact direction and subsurface impact-melt deposits.

Shock effects

Understanding shock-induced demagnetization and changes in magnetic properties of crystalline target rocks.

Planetary magnetism

Exploring implications of impact-related magnetic records for planetary magnetic-field evolution.

Field & laboratory integration

Combining field-based geological investigations with laboratory magnetometry, XRD and magnetic data analysis.

Publications & conference abstracts

Publication · 2026

Shock demagnetization in an ambient magnetic field at the Dhala impact structure, India

Communications Earth & Environment. First-author publication. The study examines how impact-generated shock waves modify remanent magnetization in unshocked rocks, monomict breccia and impact melt rock.

View DOI →
Publication · 2024

The probable direction of impact at Dhala impact structure, India

Earth, Planets and Space. Co-authored study using microfracture intensity and X-ray diffractometry to infer the probable southwest-to-northeast impact direction.

View DOI →
Publication · 2024

Tectonic development in Singhbhum Craton, NE India decrypted from dyke swarms

Physics of the Earth and Planetary Interiors. Study of dyke-swarm magma dynamics, paleostress and crustal extension in the Singhbhum Craton.

View DOI →
Conference abstract · AGU 2025

Rock Magnetic and Paleomagnetic Study of Target Rocks and Impactites from the Dhala Impact Structure, India

GP21A-VR8989. The abstract compares paleomagnetic behaviour of unshocked target rocks, monomict breccia and impact melt rock at Dhala.

View abstract →
Conference abstract · EGU 2026

Shock Effects on Magnetic Remanence in Rocks from the Dhala Impact Structure, India

EGU26-587. The abstract evaluates shock-related changes in domain state, coercivity spectrum and remanence efficiency using AF demagnetization, IRM and ARM experiments.

View abstract →
Conference abstract · Castle Meeting 2026

Shock-induced demagnetization of target rocks at the Dhala impact structure, India

19th Biennial Castle Meeting on Rock, Paleo & Environmental Magnetism. Poster abstract focusing on shock modification of remanent magnetization and magnetic anomalies.
